_doc: One file per place. build.py renders /states/<slug>/ (kind=state) from this file. Every number must be an official published figure with its source. Amounts in US dollars. Headline is Census state + local debt (same source and definition for every state). Generated by pipeline/census_state.py.
name: District of Columbia
title: District of Columbia State & Local Debt Clock: Official Census Data
cadence: Annual. The Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances comes out about two years after the fiscal year (survey year 2024: July 2026; survey year 2023: July 2025).
next_update: The next Census figures, for survey year 2025, are expected around mid-2027, based on the last two release dates.
fiscal_year_end_note: The District's fiscal year ends September 30, so Census's survey year 2024 holds the District government's fiscal year that ended September 30, 2023. Census survey year 2024 covers each government's fiscal year that ended between July 1, 2023 and June 30, 2024; the clock dates it June 30, 2024, the end of that window.

components.label: District of Columbia government debt
components.source_name: US Census Bureau, Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances, table GS00LOCALFIN (State and Local Government Finances by Level of Government: U.S. and States: 2017-2024), Debt - Total Debt Outstanding (LF0231)
components.source_locator: District of Columbia, Government type 'Local', items LF0231 Total, LF0233 Long-term and LF0232 Short-term Debt Outstanding, survey year 2024; amounts published in $1,000
components.includes: All debt of the District of Columbia government and any special districts in it, on the Census definition used for every state. Census's tables have no separate state-government level for the District, so all of its debt is reported as local debt. Census coefficient of variation for 2024: 0.00%.

notes: Census publishes the District's debt as $22.90 billion for 2024 (coefficient of variation 0.00%) and $21.94 billion for 2023. Census has no separate state government for the District, so the whole total is local debt.

Census's figures are the newest official totals that use one definition for every state and the District, but they lag about two years, so the live clock projects from June 30, 2024. The District's own audited annual report is fresher but is not used here, so the District stays comparable with the states.

The 2023→2024 change (+4.4%) is large enough to measure and small enough to extend, so the live number continues it as a straight line from June 30, 2024. Treat it as a projection, not a reported figure.
Not included: pension and retiree-health liabilities, and the District's share of the federal debt.
legend: District of Columbia debt is reported once a year by the Census Bureau, about two years after the fact. Real borrowing happens in lumps when bonds are sold and is repaid on schedules, so the live number is a straight-line projection from the latest Census year, shown here next to the official totals.
